result:
If I could change the world in one way—truly, deeply, irrevocably—I would instill in every human being an unshakable, lived understanding that we are all inextricably connected. Not as a platitude, not as a distant ideal, but as an undeniable truth felt in the bones: that harm to another is harm to oneself, that joy shared multiplies, and that the well-being of the whole is the foundation of any individual’s flourishing.

This wouldn’t be enforced—it couldn’t be. It would simply be known, as surely as we know fire burns or water quenches thirst. From that knowing, systems of exploitation, greed, and violence would collapse not from punishment, but from obsolescence. Compassion would become as natural as breathing. Borders, hierarchies, and divisions built on fear would dissolve because they’d be seen for what they are: illusions that starve us all.

In short: I’d heal our collective amnesia about belonging. Everything else—justice, sustainability, peace—would follow.
